# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Molina Healthcare — Member Appeals
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Jordan Kimura
Member ID: W834657908
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-06 — Reference number POC-22E5C28A5F-57467**
**Service denied:** Bunion surgery (hallux valgus), CPT 28296
**Plan:** Molina Healthcare (Commercial/ACA), State of Ohio
**Governing policy:** Molina Clinical Policy 700 — Foot Surgery: Bunionectomy (https://www.molinaclinicalpolicy.com/molinaclinicalpolicy/-/media/Molina/PublicWebsite/PDF/Common/Molina-Clinical-Policy/Foot-Surgery_Bunionectomy_R.pdf)

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing Molina's denial of the bunion surgery (CPT 28296) that my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery, requested for me. The notice dated 2026-08-06 states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking Molina to reconsider that decision and to approve the surgery.

I have reviewed Molina's own published criteria in Molina Clinical Policy 700 — Foot Surgery: Bunionectomy. Below, I set out the plan's criteria in the plan's own words and point to what is in my medical records for each one. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. Age / skeletal maturity.** The policy states:

> "Member is > 18 years old, or has documented evidence of skeletal maturity"

I am [my age / date of birth — to be completed]. My surgeon's office can confirm this from my chart.

**2. Signs and symptoms attributable to the deformity.** The policy states:

> "At least ONE of the following signs/symptoms directly attributable to a hallux valgus (HV) or bunionette deformity:"

The first item on that list is:

> "Significant and persistent pain at first metatarsophalangeal (MTP) joint or fifth MTP joint"

My records document 18 months of progressive pain in the foot that is not relieved by rest. On examination, I had positive provocative testing on the affected side, and my range of motion is limited by pain.

The list also includes:

> "Clinically significant functional limitation resulting in impaired ambulation"

My records document that I cannot tolerate closed shoes, and that there is ulceration risk over the bony prominence. Because the policy requires only **one** of the listed signs or symptoms, the documented significant and persistent pain is by itself sufficient under this criterion.

**3. Conservative treatment.** The policy states:

> "Clinically significant symptoms resulting in persistent pain and functional limitation despite at least 6 months of provider directed conservative treatment (e.g., alternative or modified footwear, protective cushions or taping, foot orthotics, pharmacotherapy, and/or debridement or trimming of hyperkeratotic lesions)"

My records show provider-directed conservative treatment across several of the exact categories the policy names, over a period longer than the six months the policy asks for:

- **Pharmacotherapy:** NSAIDs for 8 months, with inadequate relief.
- **Injection:** a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-20, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- **Alternative or modified footwear and foot orthotics:** wide toe-box footwear and a custom orthotic, together with activity modification, from 2026-05-04 to 2026-06-29, with 24 visits completed. This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note.

My symptoms have persisted through all of this. My pain has been progressive over 18 months and is unrelieved by rest, and I still cannot tolerate closed shoes.

**4. Radiographic confirmation.** The policy states:

> "Diagnosis of HV or bunionette deformity with radiographic confirmation and interpretation via weight-bearing anterior/posterior and lateral views of the affected foot demonstrating ONE of the following:"

For the procedure at issue, the policy states:

> "For Bunionectomy with Corrective Osteotomy:"

and lists, among the qualifying findings:

> "20 degrees or greater HVA, indicating moderate to severe HV deformity"

> "14 degrees or greater intermetatarsal angle (IMA), indicating moderate to severe deformity"

I had weight-bearing foot radiographs on 2026-07-01. They showed a **hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees** and an **intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees**. Both measurements exceed the thresholds the plan itself publishes, and the policy requires only one of the listed findings. My imaging satisfies both.

**5. Items my submitted records may not yet address.** Two of the plan's criteria are not spoken to in the summary of records I have:

> "Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion (e.g., strong, palpable pedal pulses)"

> "No degenerative changes, absent or mild arthritis, at the MTP joint"

I am not going to characterize findings that I cannot see in my records. I am asking my surgeon's office to forward [documentation of pedal pulses / lower extremity vascular perfusion] and [the radiology interpretation regarding degenerative changes or arthritis at the first MTP joint], if these are in my chart. The policy itself contemplates this kind of exchange:

> "Molina Healthcare reserves the right to require that additional documentation be made available as part of its coverage determination; quality improvement; and fraud; waste and abuse prevention processes. Documentation required may include, but is not limited to, patient records, test results and credentials of the provider ordering or performing a drug or service."

If any specific document would resolve the denial, I would appreciate Molina telling me and my surgeon exactly what it is, so we can send it promptly.

## A note on the excerpts I have

The excerpts above are the policy language I have been able to obtain. Molina Clinical Policy 700 contains additional criteria and list items that are not reproduced in the excerpts available to me, and I have not quoted any policy text beyond what appears above. The denial notice I received does not identify which specific criterion my request was found not to meet; it states only that the procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. **I ask Molina to identify, in writing, the specific criterion or criteria from Molina Clinical Policy 700 that it applied and found unmet, and the evidence it relied on.** That would let me and Dr. Marchetti respond to the actual point in dispute rather than to a general conclusion.

## My request

Please reconsider and overturn the denial dated 2026-08-06 (reference number POC-22E5C28A5F-57467) and authorize bunion surgery, CPT 28296, as requested by Dr. Marchetti. On the criteria the plan publishes, my records document persistent pain and functional limitation attributable to the deformity, provider-directed conservative treatment over a span longer than six months in the categories the policy names, and weight-bearing radiographic measurements well above the angle thresholds the policy sets.

I also ask that:

1. My surgeon be given the opportunity to speak with the reviewing physician if that would help; and
2. I receive a written decision that states the criterion relied on and the clinical basis for it.

Per my denial notice, my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, **by 2027-02-02**. I am submitting this appeal within that window. I am mailing this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial notice. If there is another or additional way Molina would prefer that I submit this appeal, please let me know and I will follow it.

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-06 (reference POC-22E5C28A5F-57467)
- Weight-bearing foot radiograph report dated 2026-07-01
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-04 to 2026-06-29)
- Records of NSAID therapy and corticosteroid injection dated 2026-04-20
- Office notes from Dr. Marchetti, MD
- [Any additional records to be listed]

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this.

Sincerely,

**Jordan Kimura**
Member ID: W834657908
[Signature]
[Date]
[Phone number]
[Email address, if you wish to include one]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
